entities.span: Every claimed matched skill a user sees has either been independently checked by a different vendor, or is honestly marked as unverified; nothing reads as verified that was not.
No `usage_cap` migration is needed: spec 0012 already seeded `ai_check` at the sample rate of 1.0 this feature confirms.

Reuses `scoreListing()` and the concurrent dispatch shape of `scoreListings()` unchanged in their own logic; the only tested surface this feature touches is `scoreListings()`'s return type and its span attributes.

Two chained vendor calls per listing raise the worst case wait before a card settles, from `ai_scoring`'s 30 seconds alone to somewhere between 45 and 60 seconds depending on AC-6's measured `ai_check` timeout. A reader watching a slow render can wait longer than they did before this feature, in exchange for what that wait now proves.

This stays within the platform's own function timeout: Vercel's default is 300 seconds on all plans, and this repo declares no `maxDuration` override and no `vercel.json` or `vercel.ts` (verified, neither file exists), so no platform level truncation risk is added by this feature and no `maxDuration` export is needed for this worst case.

The check only covers `matchedSkills`. A fabricated claim living only in the free text `reasoning`, never named as a matched skill, is not caught by this feature (Option 2's rejected scope). This is an accepted, named gap, not a closed one.

`scoreListings()`'s return type changes from `ScoreOutcome` to `ListingOutcome`, which is a breaking change to its own existing tests and to `page.tsx`'s and `score-card.tsx`'s consumption of it, even though `scoreListing()` and the scoring logic itself are untouched.
`ai_check` has never been invoked in production; AC-6's timeout is derived from a handful of live calls made during this feature's own build, not a large sample.

A misconfigured `ai_check` tier (`usage_gate_misconfigured`, a `Failure` rather than a refusal) renders every checkable listing in a batch as AC-7's identical unverifiable note, with no page level explanation distinguishing it from an ordinary vendor outage. This is deliberately left as is: each occurrence is still reported to Sentry individually (this project's error model reports every `Failure` on construction)
rejected_spans: ,and the correct response to a misconfigured tier is fixing the configuration, not designing a UI state for a bug that should not reach a real user.

entities.span: A page level notice for this case was considered and rejected; see Follow-up.
`ai_check`'s measured timeout, once set, is a value future features reusing this tier should read from `tiers.ts` rather than assume; it is not derived from any vendor published figure.
